# FastSurfer VINN Axial

> A PyTorch model for axial brain MRI segmentation and a frozen segmentation consistency loss for MRI super-resolution, image reconstruction, and cross-modal synthesis.

The inference CLI takes one skull-stripped T1-weighted, T2-weighted, or FLAIR NIfTI volume with exactly zero outside the brain. Use the native sampling grid when the axial in-plane spacings are equal. Use `--clip` for 0.5th–99.5th percentile clipping before the CLI's per-volume nonzero-voxel z-score. The CLI uses a scale factor of 1 mm divided by the axial in-plane spacing and returns 34 anatomical labels plus background on the input grid.

The training loss is `fastsurfer_vinn.segmentation_loss.VINNSegLoss`. It takes aligned, brain-masked and normalized axial slices of shape `(B, 1, H, W)` and a scale factor supplied by the caller from the output grid. The default soft KL objective matches the frozen VINN class distributions for the reference and prediction. The original argmax-based Dice and cross-entropy objective is available with `mode="hard"`.

On 20 BrainWeb simulated T1-weighted volumes, the mean whole-volume Dice was 0.9141 for white matter and 0.9253 for gray matter. Install a PyTorch build for your device before installing the project's Python dependencies.
